voyage.name: Palace of the Parliament
voyage.price: Adults 60 lei, students 30 lei (19-26 years old, with a valid student ID), children 20 lei (7-18 years old), children under 7 free
voyage.content: The world's second largest building (after the US Pentagon), formerly named "Casa Poporului" (People's House). Building started in 1983 by Nicolae Ceaușescu and is still not completely finished (2019). It spans 12 stories, around 1,000 rooms and covers over 330,000 m². 1/9 of Bucharest was reconstructed to accommodate this magnificent massive building and its surroundings. There are 1hr 20min tours frequently which l

voyage.name: Old City
voyage.content: A part of the city's historical heart was not demolished by Nicolae Ceaușescu. The area (stretching approximately between the Dâmbovița river to the south, Calea Victoriei to the west, Calea Moșilor to the east and the Regina Elisabeta boulevard to the north) contains an assortment of middle 19th-century buildings, ruins of the Wallachian princes' medieval court, churches, bank headquarters, a few hotels, clubs, rest

voyage.name: Revolution Square
voyage.content: Site of part of the Romanian Revolution of 1989. There is a tall monument in the center of the square in memory of those who died during the revolution.

voyage.name: Arch of Triumph
voyage.content: The current arch was inaugurated in 1936, however previous arches had been here since 1878.

voyage.name: Romanian Atheneum
voyage.content: A beautiful building is home of the George Enescu Philarmonic. If you have the time, visit the interior of the building as well, as it holds a fresco that depicts scenes of the Romanian history. The building was inaugurated in 1888.

voyage.name: Victory Square
voyage.content: Big public square in the heart of Bucharest with cultural sites and an intersection of boulevards.

voyage.name: National Art Museum
voyage.alt: Muzeul Național de Artă al României
voyage.price: 24 lei for the Romanian collection, 24 lei for the European collection, or 40 lei for booth; 75% discount for pupils, students (with valid cards), Euro 26 card holders up to 30 years old, and people with disabilities; 50% discount for pensioners
voyage.content: In the building of the former Royal Palace, this museum has collections of ancient, modern and contemporary Romanian art as well as exhibitions of rare European art dating as early as the 14th century

voyage.name: Aviation Museum
voyage.address: Fabrica de Glucoza (Șoseaua Fabrica de Glucoză) street, 4, in District 2
voyage.content: Open-air display of various types of aircraft. The museum is closed for renovation from 1 September 2023 and is expected to be closed for 30 months (until 2026).

voyage.name: National Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.hours: Cafe, 4th floor: Open: Tue-Sun 10:00-18; Library (Libraria Jumatatea Plina): Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00; Annex NMCA. Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00. Address: Mosilor 64-68, free entry; Dalles Hall (SALA Dalles) Open: Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00; Address: 18 Avenue N. Balcescu
voyage.content: Inside a converted wing of the Palace of the Parliament, in what had been the private apartments of Ceaușescu, the museum features fresh exhibitions from Romania's burgeoning art scene.

voyage.name: Curtea Veche Museum
voyage.content: The ruins of the crown palace of the Wallachian princes, some parts dating as early as the 16th century. It’s around an earlier fortification in this place that Bucharest began to develop.

voyage.name: Cotroceni Palace Museum
voyage.content: Has collections of objects that belonged to the former Romanian royal family. Today it is also the residence of the Romanian president.

voyage.name: Firefighters Museum
voyage.address: Bd. Ferdinand I, nr. 33 (Foișorul de Foc), sector 2
voyage.content: A 42-metre high building between Obor, Calea Moșilor and Nerva-Traian. It was used in the past as an observation tower by the firemen.

voyage.name: Village Museum
voyage.price: Adult 15 lei; pupils and students (with valid cards) 4 lei; pensioners and Euro 26 card holders 8 lei
voyage.content: An open air museum created in 1934, it now has around 300 traditional buildings (including churches, workshops, mills) and furniture, pottery, clothing gathered from villages in every region of the country in an effort to showcase the traditional way of life of the Romanians. Occasionally hosts folkloric and traditional crafts festivals.

voyage.name: Museum of the Romanian Peasant
voyage.content: Also dedicated to the traditional way of life, it focuses mainly on traditional interior decoration, tools, clothing and artifacts. Again, it sometimes hosts folkloric and traditional crafts festivals. ; Small public museum area, with all information solely in Romanian.

voyage.name: Geology Museum
voyage.content: Has a large collection of minerals, rocks and fossils.

voyage.name: National History Museum
voyage.alt: Muzeul Național de Istorie a României
voyage.content: It's in a neoclassical late 19th-century building, and has exhibits documenting the evolution of society on Romania’s territory from the Paleolithic until today, a replica of Trajan’s Column in Rome and a very interesting collection of jewellery and bronze articles from Roman times up to the Kingdom of Romania.

voyage.name: Nicolae Minovici Folk Art Museum
voyage.alt: Muzeul de Artă Populară Prof. Dr. Nicolae Minovici
voyage.content: Also here is Museum of Old Western Art the (Muzeul de Artă Veche Apuseană Minovici). There are collections of the various works of art, such as stained glass from the 16th-17th centuries, engravings, paintings, rare books, tapestries, carpets, furniture.

voyage.name: Military History Museum
voyage.content: Has collections of weapons dating since the prehistoric times and permanent exhibitions dedicated to important military events, including the Romanian revolution of 1989, and an outdoor exhibit of relatively modern weaponry, including cannons, tanks, helicopters. Outdoor area with vehicles closed for rebuilding as of Apr 2025.

voyage.name: National Museum of Romanian Literature
voyage.alt: Muzeul Național al Literaturii Române, Casa Krețulescu

voyage.name: D. Minovici Western European Arts Museum
voyage.content: Located in a beautiful eclectic villa

voyage.name: Frederic and Cecilia Cuțescu-Storck Art Museum
voyage.alt: Muzeul de Artă Frederic Storck și Cecilia Cuțescu-Storck
voyage.content: This museum presents works of artists of the Storck family.

voyage.name: Railways Museum
voyage.content: Shows all sorts of different exhibits from different ages of the railway network. Also has a model railway.

voyage.name: National Museum of "George Enescu"
voyage.price: Adults 6 lei, seniors 2 lei, students 1.5 lei
voyage.content: Music, memorial museum.

voyage.name: National Philatelic Museum
voyage.content: Come here for stamps, stamp collections, postal items: boxes of values, old paintings, seals, horns, prints, old letters, maps postal coachmen costumes, furniture used in post offices, etc.

voyage.name: Museum of Mary and Dr. G. Severeanu
voyage.alt: Muzeul Maria și dr. George Severeanu
voyage.address: Strada Henri Coandă (fostă I.C. Frimu) nr. 26, sector 1
voyage.content: The exhibition includes a variety of objects: pieces of archeology - ancient Greek vases, statuettes of Tanagra, bronze and marble, glass Roman items, ancient Greek, Dacian Roman, Byzantine and medieval coins. Romanian and foreign orders and decorations.

voyage.name: Bucharest History Museum
voyage.price: 10 lei and 15 lei extra to take photos (not worth it)
voyage.content: Housed in a palace built in 1834, has collections related to the development of Bucharest from a small 14th-century fortress into Romania’s capital.

voyage.name: National Museum of Old Maps and Books
voyage.alt: Muzeul Național al Hărților și Cărții Vechi
voyage.content: Small, but amazing museum with maps on 3 floors. Don’t forget to borrow one of the green magnifying glasses to discover the fine print. Historical maps from 15th-20th century from the whole world with an emphasis on Romania and the Balkan Peninsula. Note that while the name mentions books too, it's almost exclusively maps on display.

voyage.name: Jewish Community History Museum
voyage.content: Housed in a beautiful mid 19th century synagogue. Documents the life of this community in the region since ancient times and through the Holocaust. Passport required to enter.

voyage.name: Grigore Antipa Natural History Museum
voyage.content: This has over 300,000 exhibits illustrating the transformations of Earth and the evolution of species.

voyage.name: Primăveri Palace
voyage.content: The former residence of Ceaușescu, incredibly opulent, one of the most fascinating places to visit in Bucharest. Book online at least a day in advance. Tours last 45 minutes and cover all the main living areas, including the mosaic surrounded swimming pool and indoor garden

voyage.name: Museum of Recent Art (MARe)
voyage.content: Modern art gallery. Only holds one exhibition at a time, and closes for a few weeks between each.

voyage.name: Curtea Veche Church
voyage.alt: Old Court Church, Biserica Curtea Veche
voyage.address: Strada Covaci and Strada Franceză, sector 3
voyage.content: The Church of the Old Princely Court, built around 1559, used to be the coronation church of the Wallachian princes.

voyage.name: Patriarchal Cathedral
voyage.content: Built in 1658. Next to it is the Mitropoliei Palace (1708) – the residence of the Orthodox Patriarch, a sort of small 'Romanian Vatican'. It’s the only church in Bucharest in which photography is prohibited

voyage.name: Stavropoleos Church
voyage.content: Built in the early 18th century, has some stunning decorative sculpture and amazing frescoes. A little jewel.

voyage.name: Colțea Church
voyage.content: The first church in Bucharest built in the Brancovenesc style (1702).

voyage.name: New St. George Church
voyage.alt: Biserica Sfântul Gheorghe Nou din București
voyage.content: Dating from the 18th century, houses the tombs of princes Constantin Brâncoveanu and Ion Mavrocordat.

voyage.name: Kretzulescu Church
voyage.content: An interesting example of the Brancovenesc style (1722).

voyage.name: Plumbuita Monastery
voyage.address: off Șoseaua Colentina, Str. Plumbuita nr. 58, sector 2
voyage.content: Built in the last half of the 16th century, it once housed the first printing house in the region (1582), today it has a religious objects museum and a large park.

voyage.name: Oțetari Church
voyage.content: The Oțetari Church is a very discreet, spiritual place, giving some religious comfort in the centre of the city. Its name means "cruet", because of the street it is on. It was built in the 18th century and it features a number of interesting paintings and stained glass.

voyage.name: Great Synagogue of Bucharest
voyage.alt: Sinagoga Mare din București, בית הכנסת הגדול של בוקרשט
voyage.content: This decorative temple was raised in 1845 by the Polish-Jewish community. It was repaired in 1865, baroque style, redesigned in 1903 and 1909, repainted in Rococo style in 1936. It hosts an exhibition on the Holocaust in Romanian. Entry by donation. Security checks require your passport

voyage.name: All Saints' Antim Monastery
voyage.content: An Orthodox monastery in Brâncovenesc style from 1715 with a church, a museum and a shop. The church, museum and shop are open to the public. The church is in the center of a courtyard with the museum and shop in buildings around the sides. The church is richly decorated with distinctive carved wooden doors. The shop sells mainly religious texts and iconography but also has a leaflet in English and other languages fo

voyage.name: Therme București
voyage.content: Huge thermal water park.

voyage.name: Cișmigiu Garden
voyage.content: This a lovely small park; it's the oldest in the city (designed 1845-1860). Has boat rental in summer, ice skating in winter time, reasonable restaurants and more specially a French restaurant in Trianon Hotel and several bars.

voyage.name: Herăstrău Park
voyage.content: The largest of several parks around man-made lakes on the Colentina River running through the city’s north and east side) houses the Village Museum, an open-air theater, various sports grounds, an amusement park and numerous restaurants and clubs. Has boat rental and boat-trips in summer.

voyage.name: Botanical Gardens
voyage.content: Established in 1860, displays a variety of plants from all over the world. The greenhouses are wonderful but have limited opening hours, and are closed Monday, Wednesday and Friday

voyage.name: Carol Park
voyage.content: Designed in 1906, Carol Park has an open-air theater replicating a Roman arena and another construction replicating a medieval fortress. It houses the tomb of the Unknown Soldier as well as an infamous mausoleum built for the Communist nomenclature.

voyage.name: Tineretului Park
voyage.content: It has a large multipurpose building (Sala Polivalenta) used for concerts, sporting events, exhibitions, etc., an amusement park for children, boat-rental, several restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Titan Park
voyage.content: A green oasis among Communist-era high-rise apartment buildings in the eastern part of the city (Titan metro station), has a charming wooden church as well as several lakeside clubs.

voyage.name: Filarmonica George Enescu
voyage.content: Housed in the Romanian Atheneum, a city landmark.

voyage.name: Teatrul Național de Operetă Ion Dacian
Sala Radio
voyage.content: A concert hall that plays an important role in the country's classical music life. Built in 1959 and opened in 1961, it is the country's largest symphonic concert hall.

voyage.name: Cinemateca Română
voyage.content: A branch of the National Film Archives, screens mostly classic movies.

voyage.name: Noul cinematograf al regizorului roman
voyage.content: Art films and documentaries selected by major Romanian directors.

voyage.name: Eurocinema
voyage.content: Plays mainly independent European movies.

voyage.name: Europa
voyage.content: Plays relatively recent European movies.

voyage.name: Cinema Elvira Popescu
voyage.price: 20 lei, carnet of 5 tickets: 70 lei, children under 12: 10 lei
voyage.content: Mostly French movies.

voyage.name: Cinema City
voyage.content: Largest multiplex in the city (21 screens, including one IMAX).

voyage.name: Hollywood Multiplex
voyage.content: This was the first multiplex to open in Bucharest and has 10 screens.

voyage.name: Movieplex
voyage.content: Located in the western part of Bucharest, has 11 screens.

voyage.name: Patria
voyage.content: A large (over 1,000 seats) 1930s cinema located along the city's main avenue.

voyage.name: Scala
voyage.content: Another large older cinema in the downtown.

voyage.name: Bucharest Mall
voyage.content: The first one to be completed, in 1999.

voyage.name: Jolie Ville Galleria
voyage.address: Str. Erou Iancu Nicolae nr. 103 bis, Voluntari, judetul Ilfov
voyage.content: Mega Image hypermarket, services: Florists, pharmacies, cleaners.

voyage.name: Băneasa Shopping City
voyage.content: Opened in April 2008.

voyage.name: Liberty Center
voyage.hours: Shops: daily 10:00-22:00, supermarket: 09:00-22:00, cinema: Mon-Fri 12:00; Sat-Sun 10:00

voyage.name: Sun Plaza
voyage.hours: Gallery stores Mon-Sat 10:00-22:00, Restaurants & cafes: Sun-Thu 10:00-23:00, Fri-Sat 10:00-24:00; Cora hypermarket: Mon-Fri 8:00 -22:00

voyage.name: Promenada
voyage.content: Opened in 2014, it is one of the biggest shopping malls in Bucharest.

voyage.name: Mega Mall
voyage.content: Opened in 2015, this is the newest and one of the biggest shopping malls Bucharest has to offer.

voyage.name: Cărturești Carusel
voyage.content: Breathtaking bookstore in a restored 19th-century building.

voyage.name: Cărturești
voyage.content: A few blocks south of Piața Romană on the east side of Bd. Magheru. The store is set back the street and has a small park in front of it. +phone=+40 21 72 1518351, 788758408

voyage.name: Nautilus
voyage.content: An English-language bookstore near the Kiseleff Park, mostly with fantasy and science fiction books.

voyage.name: Anthony Frost English Bookshop
voyage.address: Calea Victorei, Nr. 45, Sector 1, Bucharest, Romania
voyage.content: An English-language bookstore. Lots of reasonably-priced books and a comics (mostly manga) section.

voyage.name: Dalles
voyage.content: Near Piața Universității (University square).

voyage.name: Kanteen 162
voyage.content: Very good food, consistent menus, impeccable service and kind staff. Best place to find the traditional taste of organic food.

voyage.name: LUCA
voyage.content: Cheap Romanian traditional pastry chain with locations all over the city (and much of Romania, and even Poland). There are both sweet and savory products. Good for vegetarians. Huge selection of pastries for all tastes. Most popular are the covrigi: tradițional, vișine, and nutella. Coffee is very cheap too. No tables.

voyage.name: SC Argentin Impex LLC
voyage.content: Very good Romanian meals, a treat for the senses. Nice quiet outdoor area.

voyage.name: Bodega "La Mahala"
voyage.content: A secluded and quiet place hidden a bit among the noisy and losing western-style pubs of the Old Town. It has an intimate and a bit old-fashioned Romanian look which gives it the feeling of the 90s with some more modern elements. The decor is nice and the food equally good. Cats are present.

voyage.name: Cuptorul cu lemne
voyage.content: A nice pizza place with a nice outdoor summer garden and a relaxed atmosphere (the restaurant also houses a caricature club). Tends to be very crowded during weekends.

voyage.name: Locanta Jaristea
voyage.content: Beautiful historically themed restaurant, live traditional music, old Romanian specialties; but always check the bill thoroughly. Reservations are compulsory.

voyage.name: Rossetya 2.0
voyage.content: Classic style restaurant with prices a bit higher than average, but with a very neat and cultivated atmosphere, outstandingly friendly English-speaking personnel, high food quality.

voyage.name: Trattoria Il Calcio Universitate
voyage.content: One of the best pizza places in the old town.

voyage.name: Restaurant Hanu' lui Manuc
voyage.content: Great location in Bucharest city centre and wonderful traditional food.

voyage.name: Caru' cu Bere
voyage.content: One of the most famous restaurants in Bucharest, in a historic building.

voyage.name: Trattoria Buongiorno
voyage.content: Trattoria Buongiorno is bringing a little piece of Italy to the middle of Bucharest.

voyage.name: Taj Indian Cuisine
voyage.content: Good Indian restaurant near Marriott hotel, especially for vegetarians.

voyage.name: Il Bocconcino - Restaurant si livrare Popesti-Leordeni
voyage.content: Italian restaurant.

voyage.name: Kanpai
voyage.content: Japanese pub/bistro.

voyage.name: Casa di David
voyage.content: Opened in 2005, it is a hangout of the city's nouveau riche. It comes complete with German car ads at the entrance and an extensive wine list. Food (Italian inspired) and ambience are OK, but portions are small and prices are far above average for Bucharest. A 3-course meal for two with local wine will set you back over 400 lei.

voyage.name: Red Angus Steakhouse
voyage.content: In the Old Center, across the street from the Old Court. The restaurant serves high quality USDA Choice beef and offers an excellent, diverse menu, for all tastes. Also at 56 Franceza St.

voyage.name: Absintherie Sixtină
voyage.content: Classic style bar with reasonable prices. The absinthe is served with a slow drip fountain.

voyage.name: Beer O'Clock
voyage.address: Gabroveni 4 and Villacrosse passage (near Police Department)
voyage.content: Bar with several types of Belgian, Czech and Slovak beer.

voyage.name: Camera din Față
voyage.content: Cafe/tea house

voyage.name: Curtea berarilor
voyage.content: Pub in old center having mostly Timișoreana beer.

voyage.name: Green Hours
voyage.content: A quiet club which often hosts jazz concerts.

voyage.name: Interbelic
voyage.content: Cocktail bar; fine spirits, great nights.

voyage.name: BEAT bar umanist
voyage.content: Nice cosy bar near Unirii/old town.

voyage.name: Hard Rock Cafe
voyage.content: Favorite of both locals and tourists, the Hard Rock Cafe makes its home on the shores of the lake, just a few short steps from the landmark Triumph Arch.

voyage.name: Mancave
voyage.content: Gaming venue that also has boardgames, specialty coffee and drinks.

voyage.name: Bamboo
voyage.content: It's the largest club in Bucharest. Upmarket and expensive.

voyage.name: Cafe Hazard
voyage.content: A rock bar, with a great atmosphere, open thinking, great beer and people.

voyage.name: Club A
voyage.content: The oldest club in Bucharest, with nearly 40 years tradition (this means amazingly much for a city where most clubs are less than 5 years old). Since the beginning, it was and remains a student pub and club, with an unpretentious but welcoming atmosphere, good music and low prices. Like many clubs in Bucharest, the bouncers can be overly aggressive to patrons at times.

voyage.name: Control Club
voyage.content: Best alternative/indie club with a lot of live shows and good music.

voyage.name: Expirat/OtherSide
voyage.content: Very lively and popular club, divided in two sections - Expirat, the old club with rock/dance/hiphop music, and its newer offspring, the OtherSide, where DJs spin electronica. Themed nights, very expat-friendly, great cocktails and very reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Fire Club
voyage.content: The most well-known rock and metal club in Bucharest. By day a pub and outdoor cafe.

voyage.name: Kulturhaus
voyage.content: A club with a German concept – ”the culture house” – a place where all sort of cultural events (such as live music concerts, art exhibitions, film projections) take place. Kulturhaus is very cheap – no entry fee (except for music concerts) and low prices – it is the cheapest club in town – maybe this is why the place is crowded every Friday and Saturday night until 05:00.

voyage.name: Queen’s Club
voyage.price: Entry 20 lei, but that includes 10 lei worth of drinks at the bar
voyage.content: Like gay clubs the world over, this place has become tremendously popular with a hetero set fed up with the meat market atmosphere at so many of the city’s other locations. That, together with superb music, makes this an essential stop for hedonists of all persuasions. Shake it. It can become quite crowded so watch yourself.

voyage.name: Underworld
voyage.content: The only punk-rock oriented pub in Bucharest. It also has a small concert hall, a fusball table, board games, dedicated evenings, etc.

voyage.name: Apartamente Regim Hotelier Bucuresti
voyage.content: Short term apartments in the city center.

voyage.name: Short Term Apartments Rental
voyage.content: Professionally managed serviced apartments in the center of the city.

voyage.name: Camping Casa Alba
voyage.content: Space for up to 80 caravans or 120 tents, running water, showers, toilets, kitchen. Next to Casa Alba restaurant.

voyage.name: Butterfly Villa Hostel
voyage.content: Clean hostel in the centre of sector 1. Bed-sheets, breakfast and internet is included the price. Airport pick-up, excursions and laundry-service.

voyage.name: Midland Hostel
voyage.content: Central, breakfast included, free internet.

voyage.name: Vila Gabriela
voyage.price: B&B double room (shared toilet) 25 EUR/night; en suite 35 EUR
voyage.content: Big house managed by a friendly couple, Carmina and Vlad. Carmina can speak English, French and Italian. The rooms are clean and welcoming.

voyage.name: Zen Tribe Hostel
voyage.address: Strada Radu de la Afumați 12B, București 020667
voyage.content: Clean and spacious hostel. Relaxed atmosphere, very friendly owner and guests with social common spaces. Comfortable beds, great showers and good location. No laundry service.

voyage.name: Carpați
voyage.content: One-star. Small rooms in a clean and welcoming atmosphere.

voyage.name: Hotel Andy
voyage.content: 3 star, small rooms, some street noise, couldn't be closer to Gara de Nord Station.

voyage.name: Hello Hotels
voyage.content: Good location for those on a budget.

voyage.name: Vienna House Easy
voyage.content: Good stay & fly option, hotel offers shuttle bus to terminal, you hardly need it.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Bucharest Airport
voyage.content: Probably even more walkable than Vienna House.

voyage.name: Ambasador
voyage.price: Single from 50 EUR, double from 60 EUR/night, breakfast included
voyage.content: 3-star in Art Deco slab, with restaurant.

voyage.name: Alia Accommodation Bucharest
voyage.content: Serviced apartments in the city center at the University Square. Metro and buses just outside the building.

voyage.name: Arkadia Apartments
voyage.content: Five whole short-stay apartments run by one operator: two 1-bedroom flats at this address, with free private parking, plus flats at Băneasa Panorama Lake, about 5 minutes' walk from Crângași metro. All have a kitchen and self check-in and are classified 3 stars by the Ministry of Tourism. Booking requests by WhatsApp; invoices issued.

voyage.name: Capitol
voyage.content: Comfortable, 100-year-old three-star hotel with big rooms and enormous bathrooms.

voyage.name: Casa Victor
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with restaurant, pool & spa.

voyage.name: Class Hotel
voyage.content: On Baneasa lakeside, 4-star hotel with restaurant, pool, spa & gym.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza
voyage.content: Business hotel.

voyage.name: Dalin Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star place with bar & restaurant.

voyage.name: Ibis Gara de Nord
voyage.content: Reliable budget chain 100 m from railway station.

voyage.name: K+K Hotel Elisabeta
voyage.content: Central.

voyage.name: Le Boutique Hotel Moxa
voyage.content: Four-star hotel, centrally located.

voyage.name: NH Bucharest
voyage.content: Modern 4-star hotel in the business district. Bedrooms are cosy and comfortable with a modern twist.

voyage.name: Novotel
voyage.content: Reliable 4-star choice. The facade is what's left of the former National Theatre.

voyage.name: Ramada Majestic
voyage.content: Handy for university.

voyage.name: Rin Airport Hotel
voyage.content: Provides spacious rooms with air conditioning, free Wi-Fi, and free access to its spa area.

voyage.name: Rin Central
voyage.content: 4* hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Siqua
voyage.content: With Italian restaurant, conference facilities.

voyage.name: Hotel Corvaris
voyage.content: Clean, handy for motorists.

voyage.name: Carol Parc Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel looking onto Carol Park.

voyage.name: Epoque
voyage.content: 5-star all-suites hotel in a quiet location just west of Cișmigiu Gardens.

voyage.name: Europa Royale
voyage.content: A four-star hotel in the Old Town.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Athénée Palace
voyage.content: 5-star hotel. Nice coffee shop, pretty garden terrace in summer.

voyage.name: Sheraton Bucharest Hotel
voyage.content: Upscale hotel, with casino & restaurants including Benihana Japanese Steakhouse.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Bucharest
voyage.content: Central 5-star high-rise block built in 1971, with restaurant and swimming pool.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Bucharest Grand
voyage.content: Large hotel behind the Parliament building. 4 restaurants, bar, spa & sauna.

voyage.name: Opera
voyage.content: 3-star.

voyage.name: Phoenicia Grand Hotel
voyage.content: Upmarket place with 4 restaurants, bar, night-club, spa and gym. Very close to Baneasa Airport at north edge of Bucharest.

voyage.name: Parliament
voyage.content: Designer hotel, looking onto Parliament building

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel
voyage.content: Upmarket place with indoor & outdoor pools, 5 restaurants and 4 bars.

voyage.name: Rin Grand Hotel
voyage.content: Stylish place overlooking Lake Vacaresti at the edge of town with a restaurant and piano bar. 24-hour fitness centre with indoor pool, a whirlpool and saunas. Also with beauty salon, conference and banquet facilities, and free parking.
